tool.name: bigWigAverageOverBed
tool.description: Compute average score of a bigWig over each BED region

param.name: bigwig
param.label: bigWig signal file
param.help: For example read coverage created from a BAM file.

param.name: regions
param.label: Regions (BED)
param.help: Needs at least 4 columns, and the names in column 4 must be unique. With BED12 only the blocks (exons) are counted.

param.name: mode
param.label: Where to measure the signal
param.option: In a window around the centre of each region

param.label: Window width (bases)
param.help: The window is centred on the middle of each region and replaces the region itself.

param.label: Report minimum and maximum
param.help: Adds two columns with the lowest and highest value seen in each region.

param.label: Add a header line
param.help: Writes the column names as the first line of the summary table.

param.name: out_bed
param.label: Regions with the mean appended
param.help: (-bedOut) A copy of the input regions with the mean as an extra column.

param.name: out_stats
param.label: Overall statistics
param.help: (-stats) Totals over all regions, such as the share of the total signal that falls inside them.

tool.help:
**What it does**
`bigWigAverageOverBed`_ summarises the signal of a bigWig file over each region of a BED file. It reports one line per region, for example the read coverage of every gene in one sample.
**Inputs**
- A bigWig file with the signal, for example coverage made from a BAM file. - A BED file with the regions. It needs at least 4 columns and the names in column 4 must be unique. If the file is BED12, only the blocks (exons) are counted and the gaps between them (introns) are skipped.
**Output**
A table with one row per region:
======= ======================================================================= Column Meaning ======= ======================================================================= name name of the region (column 4 of the BED file) size number of bases in the region (sum of the block sizes for BED12) covered number of those bases that have data in the bigWig sum sum of the signal over the covered bases mean0 sum / size, so bases without data count as zero mean sum / covered, the average over the covered bases only ======= =======================================================================
``covered / size`` gives the breadth of coverage of a region and ``mean0`` its average depth. With *Report minimum and maximum* two more columns, ``min`` and ``max``, are added.
**Note on the "covered" column**
``covered`` counts bases that have *any* value in the bigWig, including an explicit zero. If the bigWig stores zeros for bases without reads, ``covered`` always equals ``size`` and every region looks fully covered. To measure breadth of coverage, create the bigWig without those zeros, for example with the *Skip non-covered regions* option of bamCoverage.
**Additional outputs**
- *Regions with the mean appended*: the input regions with the ``mean`` as an extra last column (followed by ``min`` and ``max`` if requested). - *Overall statistics*: totals over all regions, such as the fraction of the total signal that lies inside the regions (``spotRatio``).
For implementation details see the `source code`_.
.. _bigWigAverageOverBed: http://hgdownload.cse.ucsc.edu/admin/exe/linux.x86_64/FOOTER.txt .. _source code: https://github.com/ucscGenomeBrowser/kent/blob/master/src/utils/bigWigAverageOverBed/bigWigAverageOverBed.c
